brief: Goldman's Pasquariello frames a tug-of-war: Treasury yields have surged (2-year up 145bps YTD, 10-year at levels last seen in 2007), hurting zero-yield assets like gold, while the S&P has been range-bound near 7700 and rate-sensitive sectors (biotech, small caps, REITs, homebuilders, utilities, non-profitable tech) have drawn down 8-19%. Yet the index sits near all-time highs because mega-cap tech (citing Meta's Muse, Nvidia's buyback) has powered ahead. Breakevens have barely moved even as 10-year yields rose for seven straight months, so he argues inflation, not a 2022-style driver, is behind the backup; instead P/E has compressed (23x to 19x year over year, per Ben Snider) while earnings growth offset it, keeping the earnings-yield/10-year spread steady. Bears note a historical 2-standard-deviation yield-backup rule just triggered; bulls counter with 1999, when NDX rallied 61% even as the Fed kept hiking. His base case: higher rates are a headwind, not a wrecking ball, absent an inflation surge or credit seizure (unlike 2007). He stays long equities and commodities, short fixed income via options, and likes cheap tail hedges on stress-sensitive sectors.
